:::{#exm-strong-induction}
#### Every term of the Fibonacci sequence is less than a power of 2

Let $F_1, F_2, \ldots$ be the [Fibonacci sequence](#def-fibonacci-sequence).
To prove $F_n < 2^n$ for every $n \in \Nat$,
let $P(n)$ be the [inequality](proof-writing.qmd#def-inequality) $F_n < 2^n$
and use @def-strong-induction with $n_0 = 1$.

**[Base cases](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-induction), $n = 1$ and $n = 2$.**
The step below uses the two entries $F_{n-1}$ and $F_{n-2}$ before $F_n$,
which do not exist for $n = 1$ and $n = 2$,
so these two cases are shown directly:

$$
\ba
F_1 &= 1 < 2 = 2^1
&& \text{(} 1 < 2 \text{)}
\\
F_2 &= 1 < 4 = 2^2.
&& \text{(} 1 < 4 \text{)}
\ea
$$

**Step of the [strong induction](#def-strong-induction), $n \ge 3$.**
Let $n \ge 3$, and suppose $P(k)$ holds for every [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers) $k$ with $1 \le k < n$.
Then $k = n - 1$ and $k = n - 2$ both satisfy $1 \le k < n$,
so $F_{n-1} < 2^{n-1}$ and $F_{n-2} < 2^{n-2}$.
Therefore

$$
\ba
F_n
&= F_{n-1} + F_{n-2}
&& \text{(definition of } F_n \text{, since } n \ge 3 \text{)}
\\
&< 2^{n-1} + 2^{n-2}
&& \text{(strong induction hypothesis, twice)}
\\
&< 2^{n-1} + 2^{n-1}
&& \text{(} 2^{n-2} < 2^{n-1} \text{)}
\\
&= 2 \cdot 2^{n-1}
&& \text{(} a + a = 2a \text{)}
\\
&= 2^n,
&& \text{(} 2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^n \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is $P(n)$.
By @def-strong-induction,
$F_n < 2^n$ for every $n \in \Nat$.

:::
